$schema: DEP-018 — the campaign fault matrix. Its invariants are scripts/lib/campaign-fault-matrix.mjs; its checker is scripts/check-campaign-fault-matrix.mjs, whose reds are scripts/check-campaign-fault-matrix.test.mjs. The M1-D1-SPINE cases are injected by tests/d1/m1-fault-matrix.test.mjs on the D1 stack with the DEP-016 one-worker override; the D2 profiles' cases are keyed and their runs are the planning session's to dispatch (founder ruling F8).
$fields: case = the id, unique across profiles. family ∈ fault_control|restart_reconciliation|cancellation|provider_failure|cleanup|credential|redaction|tenant. injection.mechanism = WHAT is injected; injection.observedBy = the probe whose result decides whether it FIRED (acceptance 1: a case whose injection did not fire is a failure, not a pass). expectedClassification = the outcome the campaign requires. tenantCase = the F10 matrix entry. credentialCase = the E5 exit-gate clause-4 lease-scoped redemption-refusal entry (kind ∈ lease_expired_redemption_refused|wrong_lease_redemption_refused, each with a same-tenant positiveControl). redactionCase = the E5 clause-5 entry (a plantedCanary, an unseededControl that leaks verbatim, the streams the marker is asserted on, and the producer whose scrubbing is proven). evidence = required|pending; a pending case carries pendingKind (keyed|structural), pendingReason and pendingOwner, is never a pass, and reds if a bundle reports evidence for it.

profiles.$topology: docker-compose.d1.yml + docker/d1/m1-spine.override.yml — ONE control plane, ONE worker container, the DEP-016 F10 tenant set (two enabled Organizations A and B, one control C). Keyless: the reference provider (packages/sandbox-fake-provider) and Toxiproxy are the only fault substrates, and no E2B key is ever needed.

injection.target: worker-to-control-plane
injection.observedBy: a REAL worker request through the Toxiproxy LISTEN address a worker uses (toxiproxy:13100) succeeds before the cut, FAILS during it, and succeeds after the restore -- the fault is load-bearing on the path under test, not merely visible on a side probe. The reap still reaches the control plane directly, deliberately: it is the operator's path, and routing it through the cut would prevent the reclaim this case observes. The reconnected worker's late ack must then be denied 409 with a non-disclosing fence code (measured: attempt_terminal), not merely be non-200 -- the route also emits 503 internal_unavailable, which would otherwise pass as a reclaim.

injection.target: control-plane-to-postgres
injection.observedBy: a raw TCP connect to the toxiproxy listen port (toxiproxy:15432) is REFUSED while cut and connects after restore (measured rather than an HTTP probe: this link carries the PostgreSQL wire protocol, which probeProxyReachable cannot speak, and the test-runner image has no postgres client). The classification ALSO requires the outage response, measured with an ENROLLED worker and a VALID session so the request reaches the DB-backed admission limiter and leasing service (an invalid session is refused by verifyWorkerOperationProof before either): the SAME poll succeeds 200 while the database is up and FAILS CLOSED while it is severed -- either 429 throttled, which is the admission limiter's own documented shared-store-error contract, or a 5xx -- and never answers an offer. Both renderings are accepted so a correct 429 cannot red the lane; the one answer excluded is the defect, a 2xx.

injection.target: worker-to-minio
injection.observedBy: the presigned PUT through the throttled link either throws or returns non-2xx (putPresignedBytesAllowError). The classification then requires the EXACT protocol rejection -- 200 with {outcome: rejected, reason: malformed|event_hash_mismatch} -- so a 500 or a crashed commit route cannot be read as a successful refusal.

injection.target: control-plane
injection.observedBy: the container's State.StartedAt advances across the restart and its docker health returns to healthy. The classification compares the attempt AND lease rows byte-for-byte across the restart, not merely the lease's existence, so a lease whose status moved would red.

injection.target: leases.expires_at
injection.observedBy: expireLeaseDeadlines reports updated === 1 — the deadline row was actually moved

injection.target: worker-b
injection.observedBy: the startup reconciler's own FENCED arm in worker-b's container log, attributed THREE ways: (1) the fence line is ABSENT before the kill and PRESENT after it, compared by OCCURRENCE COUNT rather than presence so an earlier boot in the retained tail cannot satisfy it; (2) it carries THIS run's lease id; (3) NEITHER sibling arm of the same three-way branch (candidate pruned / nothing renewed) names this lease. The structured reason lease_candidate_fenced is asserted beside the message. The probe is exactly one lease_renew, so leases.expires_at moves and the lease is still live afterwards -- recorded as corroboration, not attribution, because the pre-kill renewal loop moves the same column. ★ A FOURTH arm exists but is BANKED ACROSS RUNS rather than re-earned here, and a reader should know which: a SAME-MECHANISM negative control, in which the identical in-flight run interrupted by a GRACEFUL restart reports lease_candidate_store_empty and adds NO fence line -- passed in full on runs 35956091950, 35957846155, 35960080927 and 35962071988. It is not in this case because a SECOND worker interruption lapses the session past the WRK-010 section 3.2 enrolment code-route boundary and this lane's one-time ticket is consumed (measured on run 35964102214: eligibility probe failing:[], seenRecently false). Attribution here is therefore genuinely weaker by one arm, which is stated rather than glossed.

cases.pendingReason: MEASURED LIVE over seven campaigns on this branch, and the LAST TWO are what make it structural rather than a design flaw of the driver. Run 35964102214 (the eligibility probe) returned failing:[] -- the attempt satisfied ALL ELEVEN lease-candidate conjuncts, with no rejection certificate and no capacity pressure -- while workers[0].seenRecently was FALSE: the attempt was fully eligible and the worker was not polling. Run 35966651671 then tried the SINGLE-INTERRUPTION redesign that had been the outstanding untried option: the attempt WAS leased on poll 1 and the injection DID fire, and still NO startup-reconcile arm appeared and leases.expires_at never moved. THE CAUSE, from the worker's own log: after a kill it boots "already enrolled; skipping control-plane enrollment" -> "worker session terminal: operator re-enrollment required (fresh enrollment code needed)" (enroll_unauthorized, HTTP 401) -> "session terminal at boot; running idle" -> "its session lapsed past the enrolment code-route boundary -- WRK-010 section 3.2". The startup reconciler runs INSIDE composeDispatchRuntime, and composition is only reached on the branch where a session was established, so a worker that comes back WITHOUT one never runs the reconciler at all. This lane's enrolment ticket is ONE-TIME and already consumed, so nothing here can supply the fresh code the daemon asks for. IT IS THE LANE, NOT THE PRODUCT: the daemon does exactly what WRK-010 section 3.2 documents and says so in plain words; that is deliberately NOT filed as a defect. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: a lane whose worker can re-establish a session after a restart -- a renewable or re-issuable enrolment ticket, or a session TTL that outlives a campaign. UNSEPARATED, AND SAID SO: exactly when the session lapses relative to a campaign's start is not measured; run 35966651671's two boots are ten minutes apart. ★ The reason is PROVEN LIVE AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by the test "THE RECONCILE BLOCKER, measured live" in tests/d1/m1-fault-matrix.test.mjs, which records nothing, parks a real run in flight so a candidate row EXISTS, and REDS if the killed worker ever re-establishes a session or if a startup-reconcile arm ever appears -- so this declaration cannot outlive its reason unnoticed. NOT CLAIMED: that the case is unbuildable anywhere. It is unbuildable ON THIS LANE.

the run's event stream and the worker's container log are scanned for the canary (redeemed through synthesiseRunSecrets and registered as a redaction canary), which must be ABSENT, and for the scrubber's OWN replacement marker REDACTION_MARKER = « redacted » (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/redaction.ts, substituted FOR the canary by scrubEventStrings), which must be PRESENT. Each stream's observed byte length must be non-zero. Neither arm passes alone: a clean stream with no marker may be a run that emitted the value nowhere, and a marker with the canary still present is a partial scrub. Remove the redaction and BOTH arms flip.

cases.$supersededPendingReason: MEASURED LIVE over three full campaigns on this lane (runs 35933605253, 35936498467, 35938378052): the redeemed credential NEVER appears on the run event stream or the deployed worker container log, and neither does the scrubber own REDACTION_MARKER. So a clean stream here is VACUOUS -- scrubEventStrings has nothing to substitute -- and reporting it as a scrub would be the failure this case exists to prevent. Cause: the reference provider executes a deterministic scripted transcript (packages/sandbox-fake-provider/src/scripted-command.ts) that is a pure function of (args, usage), never reads the sandbox env, and passes over any argument outside the --aoa-fake- namespace without comment. UNBUILT HERE, NOT UNAVAILABLE -- stated that way deliberately, because "unavailable" is what the two wrongly-excused spine cases claimed. It needs ONE --aoa-fake-echo-env=<NAME> scripting flag on the reference provider, a provider-package change with its own typecheck and build. ★ The reason is PROVEN LIVE and in BOTH directions by the test "THE CLAUSE-5 BLOCKER, measured live" in tests/d1/m1-fault-matrix.test.mjs, which asserts non-vacuity first and REDS if the canary or the marker ever appears -- so this declaration cannot outlive its reason unnoticed. Routed to M1a-D2-MECHANISM, where DEP-017 env probe already performs the planted execute whose echo the scrubber catches.

cases.$supersededPendingReason_DEP021: SUPERSEDED AND REPLACED by DEP-021 on 2026-09-24, because the previous reason named a FIX THAT DOES NOT WORK, and a pendingReason whose named remedy is false is the same defect class (SPINE-MATRIX-3) as a pendingReason whose blocker is false. The blocker itself STILL HOLDS and is unchanged: nothing on this lane emits the redeemed value, so scrubEventStrings has nothing to substitute and a clean stream here is VACUOUS. What is corrected is the remedy. MEASURED AT SOURCE, the whole chain: (1) an --aoa-fake-echo-env flag could only emit through ExecuteInput.onStdout, the port's one output channel; (2) that callback is the adapter-manager's own capture -- executeRelayingStdout (packages/adapter-manager/src/server.ts) builds createRunOutputCapture with canaries taken from the execute input's env VALUES, which is exactly the set the echoed value belongs to, and returns ONLY the scrubbed stdoutTail, so the raw value never crosses the wire; (3) the daemon's supervisor scrubs the tail AGAIN with the run's own canaries; (4) the tail's ONLY consumer is createUsageObserver (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/usage-observer.ts), whose composed observeRun returns {usage} -- four integers -- and NEVER populates obs.logs, the one field supervisor.ts turns into a log event. So the scrubber's marker terminates in an integer parser and reaches NEITHER declared stream. (5) That is not an oversight to be coded around: the parsed-counts log (PARSED_USAGE_LOG_MESSAGE / parsedUsageLogFields) that WOULD have carried it was built and then DROPPED by the M1 planning session (F2, 2026-09-23) after five Codex P1s of one family, filed as E4-F019, and usage-observer.ts records the consequence in its own words: "Redaction wins over diagnostics", with supervisor.ts adding "acceptance 1(b) is not live-provable". (6) The DEP-017 probe is not an alternative surface either: envProbeLogMessage serialises a summary of DIGESTS (envProbeExpectedDigests), never a value, so no canary and therefore no marker can appear in it. CONCLUSION: this case is blocked one layer DEEPER than an echo flag. It needs an observable channel for scrubbed run output on a D1 stream, which is precisely what ruling F2 deleted -- so unblocking it is a DECISION to revisit that ruling, not a build task, and DEP-021 declines to smuggle one in by adding a secret-echo capability whose every consumer discards it. The live two-directional proof of the blocker (the test "THE CLAUSE-5 BLOCKER, measured live" in tests/d1/m1-fault-matrix.test.mjs) is UNCHANGED and still reds the day either the value or the marker appears.

cases.$supersededPendingReason: Needs a real E2B run whose redeemed credential is a planted canary. ★ THE ECHO MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS ON THIS LANE, which is what makes the case provable here rather than on D1: DEP-017 env probe performs a "planted execute, so any echo of them is scrubbed" (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/env-probe.ts), and the M1a-D2-MECHANISM a2 record measured plantedControl.red: true with three canaries each detected as its expected class -- that IS the echo being caught. What is still missing is a case asserting that the run OWN event and log streams carry the scrubber REDACTION_MARKER and not the value. NOTE the lane existing "Scan the evidence AND the job log for job secrets" step is NOT this case: it scrubs the uploaded bundle, seeds no per-run canary, and has no control (E5 exit-gate audit a2 section 4, clause 5). The keyless D1 mirror is blocked on a reference-provider echo flag -- see d1.redaction.planted_canary_scrubbed. CORRECTED BY DEP-021, 2026-09-24: the final sentence above -- "The keyless D1 mirror is blocked on a reference-provider echo flag" -- is FALSE, and is superseded rather than deleted. An echo flag is necessary but NOT sufficient there: measured at source, the echoed value would be scrubbed by the adapter-manager's own createRunOutputCapture before it crossed the wire, scrubbed again by the supervisor, and then handed to createUsageObserver, which returns four integers and never populates the obs.logs field that becomes a log event -- because the log that would have carried it was DROPPED by ruling F2 (2026-09-23, filed E4-F019). So the D1 mirror is blocked on a DECISION about that ruling, not on a provider flag. THIS case, on the keyed lane, is unaffected: the DEP-017 probe's planted execute is a real echo whose detection the mechanism a2 record already measured, and what remains missing here is still only the case that asserts the run's own streams.

cases.$supersededPendingReason_DEP022: SUPERSEDED IN PLACE BY DEP-022, 2026-09-24 (the previous text is kept verbatim in $supersededPendingReason and is NOT deleted). Its remedy -- "a keyed run asserting the run's own streams" -- is FALSE, for the same reason DEP-021 measured on the D1 twin, and the blocker is one layer deeper than a keyed run. Re-measured at source on THIS lane's code path, at this revision, link by link rather than inherited: (1) an echo's only channel out of a sandbox is ExecuteInput.onStdout (packages/sandbox-provider/src/provider.ts, the per-op port); (2) on THIS lane that callback IS createRunOutputCapture, composed by executeRelayingStdout (packages/adapter-manager/src/server.ts), whose canaries are Object.values(env) -- so a planted credential is one of them -- and which returns only the SCRUBBED stdoutTail; the E2B provider runs behind the SAME adapter-manager as the reference provider, so nothing about a keyed run changes this link; (3) the daemon scrubs that tail again (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts, the observeRun call site); (4) the tail's ONLY consumer is createUsageObserver (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/usage-observer.ts), which returns { usage } -- four integers -- and never populates obs.logs, the one field the supervisor turns into a log event; (5) the log that WOULD have carried it was built and then DROPPED by the M1 planning session under ruling F2, 2026-09-23, filed E4-F019, whose own in-code note records "acceptance 1(b) is not live-provable"; (6) the DEP-017 env probe is no alternative surface on this lane either -- envProbeLogMessage serialises NAMES and DIGESTS (envProbeExpectedDigests, packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/env-probe.ts), never values, so neither the canary nor the scrubber's REDACTION_MARKER can appear in it. The superseded text's claim that "the DEP-017 probe's planted execute is a real echo whose detection the mechanism a2 record already measured" is true about DETECTION inside the sandbox and false about the two declared STREAMS, which is what this case asserts on. So the scrubber's marker terminates in an integer parser and reaches NEITHER `events` NOR `logs`, and no keyed run can make it appear. Unblocking this is a DECISION to revisit F2, not a build task; DEP-022 therefore leaves the case pending, with the measurement above as its reason, rather than flipping it to `required` on optimism and spending a keyed run to learn it.
cases.pendingReason: SUPERSEDED IN PLACE BY DEP-023, 2026-09-24 (DEP-022's text is kept verbatim in `$supersededPendingReason_DEP022` and is NOT deleted). Its measurement was correct and its conclusion -- "unblocking this is a DECISION to revisit F2, not a build task" -- has been ACTED ON. DEP-023 built the safe half of the surface F2 removed and PROVED it keylessly on the D1 twin, which is now `required`: a bounded, opt-in, tagged line of the already-scrubbed run output reaches both declared streams, with the `events` half scrubbed at `EventSequencer.#emit` and the `logs` half scrubbed at the pino DESTINATION (`createRedactingDestination`, E4-F019 closure route 2). Links 1-4 of DEP-022's chain are UNCHANGED and are the same code on this lane -- the E2B provider runs behind the same adapter-manager, so the two capture scrubs and the fail-closed refusal are identical -- and link 5's premise ("the log that would have carried it was DROPPED") no longer holds. WHAT STILL BLOCKS THIS CASE is therefore no longer structural and no longer a decision: it is that the M1a-D2-MECHANISM driver must plant a canary and assert the two arms on a KEYED run, and DEP-023 is forbidden from dispatching one (M1-AGENT-RULES hard limits; ruling F8 owns the keyed envelope). Flipping it without such a run would be a declaration of coverage nobody measured, which is the failure class this matrix exists to stop. `pendingKind` is accordingly `keyed`, not `structural`.
